headline: Day two exported the damage — Asia down 6%, the dollar re-bid, Brazil at z=3 — while Brent's 17% weekly collapse quietly handed the Fed and the consumer the only offset on the board.
summary: The US liquidation did not extend; it emigrated. VIX actually fell 3.7% to 27.14 and SKEW slipped again, but overnight Asia paid: Nikkei -6.0% (-18.0% on the month, z=-3.66), KOSPI -6.0% (-25.6% on the month), Taiex -4.5% (-20.3%). The second leg came through FX, which is new versus yesterday: DXY +0.5% to 102.03 (91st percentile), EURUSD -0.6% to 1.1171 at the 5th percentile of its year, AUDUSD -1.8%, AUDJPY -1.8% to 108.86, USDKRW +1.4% to 1359, USDCAD +0.7%. Yesterday's shock was a US equity-factor event; today it is a global funding event. Risk regime holds at -20 with credit & vol at -70, but the composition rotated — dollar composite -22 is doing work the VIX is no longer doing.

The genuinely new macro input is crude. Brent 97.70, -16.9% on the week; WTI 90.16, -13.4%; RBOB -17.1% on the week and -15.1% on the month at z=-1.45. Press ties it to US-Iran peace talks accelerating after the midterm result, with tanker incidents near Hormuz producing the bounces. That is an eight-month war premium draining, and the rates market has already monetised it: 5y breakeven -21bp on the week to 2.26 (18th percentile), 10y breakeven 2.24 (19th percentile), 2y 4.46 (-33bp on the month), 5y 4.59 (-44bp), 10y real yield 2.60 (-31bp). Cheaper fuel plus a priced-in cutting cycle is the single most constructive thing in this digest — and it is why the equal-weight tape refuses to break.

But duration still will not hedge equities. The 30y sits at 5.25% and only gave back 39bp on the month while the 5y gave 44bp; TLT rose 0.2% on a 4.4% S&P day, mortgages are 7.18% at the 85th percentile, and MOVE is +4.3% and 25% above its 200-day. 2s10s at 38bp is the 33rd percentile. This is a growth scare with a stubborn term premium, which means the equity cushion has to come from earnings, not discount rates. Inside equities the dispersion is historic: SOXX -32.9% on the month (z=-3.53), MTUM z=-4.15, high-beta/low-vol -26.4% on the month at z=-4.05, growth/value at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks — against XLP +11.6%, XLV +10.7%, IHI +15.9%, HD +22.1%, MCD +19.6% (z=3.83), WMT +19.1%, UPS +19.3%. RSP/SPY at z=4.23 with acceleration 4.20 is still the most extreme reading in the dataset.

Two things to watch rather than admire. First, credit: HYG 77.28 at the 32nd percentile of its year, HYG/IEF -3.1% on the month at z=-2.15 and rolling over, BKLN -0.7%. Spot HY price is pretending; the ratio is not. If HY starts discounting what VIX3M at 25.55 already has, the breadth cushion goes with it. Second, EM is bifurcating violently and tradeably: USDBRL +0.8% to 5.5019, +10.4% on the month at z=3.02 with acceleration 2.59, EWZ -26.1% on the month, Bovespa z=-3.79 — versus Sensex +2.2% today, +8.8% on the week, +11.5% on the month with USDINR -2.6% at z=-2.55, and Mexico's IPC at the 95th percentile. EEM/SPY at z=-2.35 masks a 40-point performance gap inside the index. Trade the dispersion, not the aggregate.

good.text: Crude's war premium is draining: Brent -16.9% and gasoline -17.1% on the week, dragging 5y breakevens 21bp lower to 2.26 (18th percentile). A real-income tailwind and a green light for cuts in one move.
The front end has fully repriced easing: 2y 4.46 (-33bp/1m), 5y 4.59 (-44bp), 10y real yield 2.60 (-31bp). Rate relief is arriving even as equities de-rate.
Breadth cushion intact and extreme: RSP/SPY z=4.23 with acceleration 4.20, equal-weight +2.1% on the month, XLP at the 96th percentile, SPLV at the 90th, KIE at the 94th.
Vol did not extend: VIX -3.7% to 27.14 despite a 6% Nikkei drop, and SKEW -1.0%. The body of the distribution was repriced yesterday; nobody is bidding new tails today.
India and Mexico have decoupled cleanly: Sensex +2.2% today and +11.5% on the month (z=2.77, acc 2.87), USDINR -2.6% at z=-2.55, IPC +8.8% on the month at the 95th percentile.
Dispersion inside tech is a gift, not just a wreck: software/semis +25.8% on the month (z=3.56) and financials relative strength +13.2%, with KRE/SPY turning up at z=1.34.

bad.text: Asia caught down hard overnight: Nikkei -6.0%, KOSPI -6.0%, Taiex -4.5%, with EWY -29.4% and EWT -27.0% on the month. The semis unwind is now a sovereign-equity event.

The dollar is re-bid into the stress: DXY +0.5% to 102.03 (91st percentile), EURUSD at the 5th percentile, AUDUSD -1.8%, AUDJPY -1.8%, USDKRW +1.4%. Accelerating dollar strength is a tightening, not a tell.
Brazil is a disorderly unwind and getting faster: USDBRL +10.4% on the month at z=3.02 with acceleration 2.59, EWZ -26.1%, Bovespa z=-3.79. Classic EM capitulation mechanics.
Credit's ratio keeps leaking while price pretends: HYG/IEF -3.1% on the month at z=-2.15 and rolling over, HYG at the 32nd percentile, BKLN -0.7%. Credit & vol composite at -70.
Momentum and leverage are being destroyed, not corrected: MTUM z=-4.15, high-beta/low-vol z=-4.05, growth/value at the 0th percentile, ARKK -19.2% and IPO -20.8% on the month.
Long duration still refuses to hedge: 30y at 5.25%, mortgages 7.18% at the 85th percentile, MOVE +4.3% and 25% above its 200-day, TLT +0.2% on a 4.4% S&P down day.

trades.name: Software over semis
trades.line: Long IGV / short SOXX: software is not a semis derivative
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SOXX, dollar-neutral; or long IGV calls vs short SOXX calls, 1-3 month tenor.
trades.thesis: The AI capex repricing is a hardware/power problem. Semis carry inventory, fabs and Asia FX risk; software carries none of it and gets a tailwind from a 44bp drop in 5y yields. The ratio is already validating: IGV/SMH +7.7% today, +25.8% on the month, z=3.56 with acceleration 2.78.
trades.trigger: SOXX -12.1% today and -32.9% on the month (z=-3.53) versus IGV -4.4% and still above its 200-day (+5.3%); SMH/SPY z=-3.99.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below its level of one week ago (-15% round trip), or IGV losing its 200-day while semis stabilise.
trades.target: Another 12-15% on the ratio; IGV relative strength vs S&P back above +10% on 1m.

trades.name: India over Korea
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EWY: the EM index is two markets now
trades.expr: Long INDA, short EWY, equal notional. Size for 2x the vol of EWY.
trades.thesis: EM is not one trade. India is a crude importer with a strengthening currency going into a cheaper-oil world; Korea is a levered semis export proxy mid-liquidation with its currency breaking.
trades.trigger: Sensex +2.2% today, +8.8% on the week, +11.5% on the month (z=2.77) with USDINR -2.6% on the month at z=-2.55; KOSPI -6.0% today, -25.6% on the month, EWY -29.4%, USDKRW +1.4% to 1359.
trades.stop: USDINR back above 95.5 or Sensex giving back its weekly gain; Korea bottoming would show as SMH/SPY turning up from z=-3.99.
trades.target: 20% on the pair over the quarter.

trades.name: High yield catch-down
trades.line: Buy HYG Dec puts: credit still hasn't paid the vol bill
trades.expr: Buy HYG Dec 76 puts financed by selling 72 puts; or short HYG vs long IEF duration-matched.
trades.thesis: Equity vol has repriced 80% in a month and HY price is down 0.3%. Credit is the last cushion holding the index together; when the ratio leads by this much the spot usually follows.
trades.trigger: HYG/IEF -3.1% on the month at z=-2.15 and rolling over while VIX sits at 27.14 (z=3.22) and VIX/VIX3M at the 100th percentile of its year; HYG at the 32nd percentile with BKLN -0.7%.
trades.stop: HYG/IEF reclaiming its 200-day with VIX back under 20; or spot HYG above 78.2.
trades.target: HYG 74.5-75; pair returns 3-4% on a duration-neutral basis.

trades.name: 2s30s steepener
trades.line: 2s30s steepener: cuts priced, term premium will not budge
trades.expr: Long TU (2y futures) vs short WN (ultra bond), DV01-matched; cash proxy is long short-duration Treasuries vs short TLT.
trades.thesis: The growth scare buys the front end; supply, sticky mortgage rates and 25%-above-trend bond vol cap the long end. Nothing in this tape rewards owning 30-year paper at 5.25%.
trades.trigger: 2y -33bp on the month to 4.46 while 30y gave only 39bp from a much higher base and TLT managed +0.2% on a 4.4% equity decline; 2s10s +6bp today to 0.38, still only the 33rd percentile; MOVE +4.3%.
trades.stop: 2s10s back below 20bp, or a 30y auction-driven rally that takes the long bond under 5.00% with MOVE falling.

trades.name: Fuel winners vs oil services
trades.line: Long JETS / short OIH as the Iran premium drains
trades.expr: Long JETS, short OIH, 1:1 notional (OIH carries more beta, so trim to 0.8x short).
trades.thesis: A peace-driven unwind of an eight-month war premium transfers margin from producers and service providers to fuel consumers. Services have the worst structure in the energy complex; airlines have the best operating leverage to a 17% weekly fuel move.
trades.trigger: Brent -16.9% and RBOB -17.1% on the week; OIH -14.8% on the week, 12.6% below its 200-day and rolling over with relative strength -5.6%/1m; JETS +3.2% on the week and turning up with relative strength +7.3%.
trades.stop: Brent back above 110 equivalent — i.e. the weekly loss fully retraced on Hormuz escalation; or JETS breaking its 200-day.

trades.name: Short the real
trades.line: Long USDBRL / short EWZ: the Brazil unwind is accelerating
trades.expr: Long USDBRL spot or 3m NDF; equity leg short EWZ outright, or buy EWZ Jan puts.
trades.thesis: A currency moving 10% in a month at z=3 with positive acceleration, alongside a 26% equity drawdown, is a positioning liquidation, not a valuation story. These rarely stop at the first round number, and a bid dollar is the accelerant.
trades.trigger: USDBRL +0.8% today to 5.5019, +10.4% on the month, z=3.02, acceleration 2.59 and turning up; Bovespa -19.3% on the month at z=-3.79; EWZ -26.1% with DXY +0.5% at the 91st percentile.
trades.stop: USDBRL back under 5.30 or EWZ reclaiming 34; a reversal in DXY below 101 also kills it.

trades.name: Fade the vol backwardation
trades.line: Sell front VIX vs buy 3-month: 100th-pctile inversion
trades.expr: Short front-month VIX future vs long Feb VIX future, 1:1; or sell a 2-week SPX strangle delta-hedged against a long 3-month put.
trades.thesis: VIX/VIX3M at 1.1029 is the 100th percentile of the past year. Full backwardation with VIX3M already at 25.55 means the term structure, not the level, is the mispricing. Carry pays while you stay hedged for a genuine credit event.
trades.trigger: VIX -3.7% to 27.14 while VIX3M held at 25.55 and SKEW fell 1.0%; the US cash index held its 200-day (+0.49% above) even with Asia down 6%.
trades.stop: VIX/VIX3M above 1.18 or a close with VIX over 35 — that means the credit leg is starting and the calendar should be cut.
